title: The graded graph cone in an etale nodal chart
statement:
Let $f:X\to T$ be a flat locally finitely presented morphism of schemes such that every nonempty geometric fibre is equidimensional of dimension one and every nonsmooth geometric fibre point has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field. Put $D=\operatorname{Sing}(f)$, the first-Fitting singular subscheme, with inclusion $i:D\hookrightarrow X$. Let $\mathcal G_f=\mathcal G(f,i)$ be the graph conormal algebra of [lem-sfb-graph-cone-gluing]. For any diagram of etale maps $U\to X$, $V\to T$ and $U\to W=\operatorname{Spec}_V\mathcal O_V[u,v]/(uv-h)$, where $h\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ and $U\to W$ is a $V$-map compatible with $f$, the singular subscheme in $U$ is
$$D_U=U\times_XD=U\times_WV(h),$$
where $V(h)\to W$ is the zero section $u=v=0$. The map $D_U\to D$ is etale. On $W$ the differential module has presentation
$$\mathcal O_W\xrightarrow{(v,u)}\mathcal O_W^2\longrightarrow\Omega^1_{W/V}\longrightarrow0,$$
so its first Fitting ideal is $(u,v)$; the presentations pull back across the etale maps to compute the Fitting singular scheme on $U$. Restriction along $D_U\to D$, followed by replacement of the ambient graph neighbourhood by $U$ and then by $W$, gives a canonical graded algebra isomorphism
$$\mathcal G_f\otimes_{\mathcal O_D}\mathcal O_{D_U}\ \cong\ \mathcal O_{D_U}[u,v]/(uv),\qquad \deg u=\deg v=1.$$
For each affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset D_U$, degree zero is $A$ and each positive degree $n$ has $A$-basis $u^n,v^n$, with mixed monomials zero and ordinary polynomial multiplication. The maps here preserve the homogeneous classes of the coordinate functions, are compatible with affine restrictions, and use the unique augmentation-preserving etale comparison at the graph, not normalization of total spaces. Such charts jointly cover $D$. Etaleness, polynomials and relative differentials are [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-polynomial-ring], [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Flatness, local finite presentation, geometric fibres, pure dimension, smoothness, completion and power series are [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The singular subscheme is [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme].

proof.text: Work over an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $B=R[u,v]/(uv-h)$. For any $B$-module $M$, an $R$-derivation $B\to M$ is exactly a pair $(a,b)\in M^2$ satisfying $va+ub=0$: assign $u\mapsto a,v\mapsto b$, extend by the polynomial Leibniz rule, and note that the derivation kills $(uv-h)$ precisely under this condition. The defining universal property of [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] therefore identifies $\Omega_{B/R}$ with $B^2/B(v,u)$. This gives the asserted presentation. By [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme], its first Fitting ideal is generated by the entries of all relation rows; those rows are the multiples of $(v,u)$, so the ideal is exactly $(u,v)$. Its quotient is $R/(h)$, including when $h$ is a unit.

source.place: Tag 00RU, lemma-differential-seq; direct universal-derivation computation of the hypersurface presentation

proof.text: Put $X_V=X\times_TV$. The projection $X_V\to X$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; hence $U\to X_V$ is etale by cancellation in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The base-change isomorphism of [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change], followed by the etale differential isomorphism of [lem-trf-formally-etale-differentials-base-change], identifies the pullback of $\Omega_{X/T}$ with $\Omega_{U/V}$. The two zero-module hypotheses needed for that differential isomorphism follow from [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] on each affine etale chart. Applying the same differential isomorphism to $U\to W$ identifies $\Omega_{U/V}$ with the pullback of $\Omega_{W/V}$. Formation of the first Fitting ideal commutes with these ring extensions by [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. Step 1 thus gives $D_U=U\times_XD=U\times_WV(h)$ scheme theoretically. Also $D_U\to D$ is etale, being a base change of $U\to X$.

source.place: Tag 0C3I, lemma-base-change-and-fitting-ideal-omega; algebra.tex Tag 0H93, lemma-formally-etale-omega; more-algebra.tex Tag 07ZA

proof.text: Write $Z=D_U$. On each affine graph neighbourhood used in [lem-sfb-graph-cone-gluing], first base change its centre from $D$ to $Z$. The ambient map is the base change of the flat map $Z\to D$ (etaleness was proved in Step 2), so [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change] identifies its conormal graded algebra with $\mathcal G_f\otimes_{\mathcal O_D}\mathcal O_Z$. Next compare the two graph neighbourhoods $U\times_V Z$ and $X\times_T Z$. The map between them is the base change of the etale map $U\to X_V$ of Step 2. There is also the etale map $U\times_V Z\to W\times_V Z$, by base change of $U\to W$. Both maps carry the graph section of $Z$ to the corresponding graph section and induce the identity on that centre. Restrict to affine neighbourhoods of each point of these sections. For either etale ring map $A\to C$, the graph augmentations give $A/I=C/J=\Gamma(Z_0,\mathcal O_Z)$ for an affine open $Z_0$ of the centre; the composite $A\to C/J$ is surjective. Thus [lem-sfb-augmented-etale-associated-graded] gives $\operatorname{gr}_I A\cong\operatorname{gr}_J C$. Inverting the comparison towards $W\times_VZ$ identifies the pulled-back graph cone with the graph cone in $W\times_VZ$.

For any affine $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Z$, Step 2 shows that $h,u,v$ restrict to zero on $Z$. Consequently $W\times_V Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}A[u,v]/(uv)$ and the graph augmentation is evaluation at $u=v=0$, with ideal $J=(u,v)$. Every polynomial modulo $(uv)$ has a unique expression $a_0+\sum_{r\ge1}a_ru^r+\sum_{r\ge1}b_rv^r$ with finite sums: remove mixed monomials; uniqueness follows because every multiple of $uv$ has only mixed monomials, whose coefficients cannot affect a constant or pure power. Hence $J^n$ for $n\ge1$ consists exactly of the sums of pure powers of degree at least $n$. It follows that $J^n/J^{n+1}$ has basis $u^n,v^n$, while degree zero is $A$. Sending the degree-one variables to their classes in $J/J^2$ therefore gives a graded algebra isomorphism $A[u,v]/(uv)\to\bigoplus_{n\ge0}J^n/J^{n+1}$: it is bijective in every degree and preserves multiplication, since mixed products vanish and pure powers multiply by addition of exponents. Invert this map and combine with Step 3.

source.place: Agent monomial calculation after Tag 0H1D; graph model supplied by curves.tex Tag 0CBY

proof.text: All maps of Step 3 are the canonical class maps $[a]\mapsto[\varphi(a)]$ of [lem-sfb-augmented-etale-associated-graded] and the class maps of [lem-pur-conormal-algebra-flat-base-change]. Their naturality identifies the maps on affine refinements; the inverses have the same compatibility. In Step 4 coefficient restriction sends each pure power to the same pure power with restricted coefficient, so it also commutes with the graded isomorphism and multiplication. The gluing identifications of [lem-sfb-graph-cone-gluing] now give the claimed sheaf isomorphism. In particular the class of each coordinate is carried to its specified degree-one class. Uniqueness here is the uniqueness of the augmentation-compatible maps on infinitesimal graph thickenings furnished by formal etaleness, not a claim that an ambient etale neighbourhood has no automorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0H1D, canonical maps and unique lifts; divisors.tex Tag 0635

proof.text: By [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], every point of $D$ is a nonsmooth point of its fibre. The hypotheses of [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model] are exactly the flatness, local finite presentation, pure one-dimensional geometric fibres and completed nodal local rings assumed here. Apply that node at each such point. It supplies a diagram of the stipulated form with a point of $U$ above it; Step 2 places that point in $D_U$. Hence these charts jointly cover $D$. When $D$ is empty the covering assertion and the local algebra assertions hold vacuously.
